Flickit build of THUG-SDL
=========================

Skate-style right stick controls for Tony Hawk's Underground (PC).
Source: the flickit branch of https://github.com/regnek/THUG-SDL

Install
-------
1. Stock THUG-SDL has to be installed and starting already
   (thugsdlpatcher.exe run once, THUG-SDL.exe launches, your controller works).
2. In the game folder, rename the existing thugsdl.dll to thugsdl.dll.bak
3. Copy thugsdl.dll from this zip into the game folder.
4. Start THUG-SDL.exe as usual.

In a level
----------
Right stick down           crouch, as deep as the stick goes (a third of the
                           way is enough; deeper = a higher ollie)
Flick away from there      ollie
Back to the centre         stand up, no ollie
Flick up-left / up-right   kickflip / heelflip (keep the stick there:
                           double, triple, if there is air for it)
Drag to the left           pop shove-it
                           (all of these with the left foot forward; with
                           the right foot forward they are mirrored)
Right stick up             crouch for a nollie, in THUG's nollie stance
Flick away from up         nollie; the flicks above, upside down, are the
                           nollie flips (up, flick down-left = nollie
                           kickflip)
Triggers                   grabs
Bumpers                    spin + nollie / spin + revert, both = get off the board
Flip or Ollie, on the ground   push (tap = a little, hold = a lot)
Right stick click          Flickit off / on (for looking around)

New in this build: room for two levels in one
---------------------------------------------
The game keeps its scripts, and every level's list of rails, objects and
restart points, in a heap of its own with fixed-size pools inside it. When
a pool is full the game crashes. New Jersey alone fills about 80% of
them; New Jersey with Manhattan joined to it would need about one and a
half times what they hold. This build makes the heap and its pools 8 times
as big before the game starts: the heap takes 31.6 MB of the 360 MB that
THUG-SDL gives the game, instead of 3.9 MB. Nothing to set; the log says:
    Memory: script memory 8 times as big: a 31.6 MB heap, ...
[Memory] BigScriptMemory=0 in thugsdl.ini leaves it as the game has it.

A test for more memory (optional, the last build)
-------------------------------------------------
For one big open world the game will need more than the 2 GB of address
space a 32-bit program gets. One bit in the exe, the large-address flag,
gives it 4 GB on a 64-bit Windows. Whether THUG copes with memory above
2 GB is what this test finds out.
  1. Close the game. Copy the three files in large-address\ into the game
     folder, next to THUG-SDL.exe.
  2. Double-click "Large address on.bat". The first time, it keeps a copy
     of the exe as THUG-SDL.exe.before-large-address.
  3. Add this to the end of thugsdl.ini:
         [Memory]
         HighMemoryTest=1
     It takes all the free address space below 2 GB while the game starts
     (reserved only, no memory behind it), so everything the game asks for
     lands above 2 GB from the first moment. Without it the game would
     only go there once a level is big enough.
  4. With [Logger] Console=1 or WriteFile=1 the log says:
         Memory: 4096 MB of address space; THUG-SDL.exe has the large-address flag
         Memory: HighMemoryTest holds ... MB below 2 GB ...
         Memory: the game's main block is 360 MB at 0x... , above 2 GB
     F9 in a level adds a line with how much of the address space is in use.
  5. Play as usual; New Jersey with the 4x texture files is a good level for
     it. A crash, a freeze or anything that looks wrong is the answer we are
     after. If something goes wrong, HighMemoryTest=0 tells whether it was
     the test.
  - Undo: "Large address off.bat", or delete THUG-SDL.exe and rename
    THUG-SDL.exe.before-large-address back.

The board's angle has its say in the grind (two builds ago)
-----------------------------------------------------------
  - Coming in at an angle, the board was swung straight for whatever the
    stick asked for: a board that looked like a crooked came down a 50-50,
    one coming in across the rail with the stick down a 5-0. In Skate the
    board meets the rail the way it comes in.
  - Now a board at an angle counts as the stick pushed the way its nose
    points ("toward" when the nose points onto the rail):
      along the rail (under 16 degrees)   the stick alone, as before
      at an angle, stick at rest          crooked when the nose points onto
                                          the rail, smith when the tail does
      at an angle, a crooked / overcrook  whichever of the two is angled
      or feeble / smith asked for         the way the board is
      at an angle, up / down / a slide    as asked: nosegrind, 5-0, slides
      across the rail (about 44 degrees)  the slides as asked; a grind on
                                          the trucks becomes a boardslide
                                          or lipslide instead of a 5-0
  - Coming onto a rail backwards along it the stick alone picks, as before.
  - GrindAngle=16 moves the line between along and at an angle (5 to 44
    degrees). GrindByBoard=0 leaves it all to the stick, as before.
  - The log line of every grind now says the board's angle to the rail,
    which end pointed onto it, and what the stick alone would have given.

No balance meter on a rail (three builds ago)
-------------------------------------------
  - Grinds and slides no longer show THUG's balance meter. The board
    cannot lose its balance on a rail, so the meter only ever sat in the
    middle.
  - Manuals and lip tricks keep their meter: their balance is still THUG's.
  - GrindBalance=1 in the [Flickit] section gives grinds THUG's balance
    back, and the meter with it.

The turn stays the trucks' (four builds ago)
---------------------------------------------
  - The turn no longer drops into THUG's sharp turn now and then. THUG
    reads Down from how far down the stick is, whatever it does to the
    side, and from 40% of the way down that is Down. So a stick pushed
    hard to one side and a quarter of the way round toward Down was
    Down + Left (or Right) to THUG, and the turn was handed to its sharp
    turn: twice THUG's own, and the trucks straight again each time the
    thumb came back up.
  - Now only how far the stick is pushed to the side turns the board, as
    in Skate. Down still brakes where THUG brakes, and still ends a push.
  - If the turning still feels wrong: Steering=0 in the [Flickit] section
    is THUG's own turning again; Steering=200 keeps the trucks and turns
    at speed about as tightly as THUG does.

Off the rail like Skate (five builds ago)
-----------------------------------------
  - When a grind runs out of speed, the board is pushed off to one side
    and the skater drops, as in Skate. Off a ledge he always goes over
    the edge, away from the top, and lands on the ground below; off a
    rail he goes to the side the board came from.
  - He leaves with Skate's speed sideways, about 1 m/s (80 units/s), so
    he drops a little way out from the ledge instead of straight down
    its side.
  - Before, he always went to his right: THUG's drop-down moves the
    skater right whichever side it is asked for (unless THUG SDL's
    directional drop-down is on), so half the time he came down on top
    of the ledge he had just left. The right bumper still does THUG's
    own drop-down, as before.
  - The movement stick no longer picks the side of this automatic exit.
  - Next to a vert ramp (a coping) he skates in, as THUG does.
  - With the console on, the log says which way he went and why:
    "Flickit: out of speed on the rail: off to his left (away from the
    ledge; a surface on his right), 80 units/s sideways".

Salads slow down on the rail (six builds ago)
----------------------------------------------
  - The FS and BS salad lost no speed on a rail: they lasted as long as
    the rail did. Now they slow down and step off like every other grind.
  - Why: THUG's scripts make the salad a grind you switch to from another
    grind with a double tap, and such a grind leaves the balance of the
    rail to the grind before it. Picked by the stick as the board lands,
    there is no grind before it, so the game balanced nothing on the rail,
    and the drag goes through that balance. Flickit now starts the balance
    for the salad the way the scripts start it for every other grind.
  - The bluntslides were not affected. With GrindBalance=1 the salad has
    the game's balance meter now, as the other grinds do.
  - With the console on, the log line for the rail says so: "salad (by
    script name; its script leaves the balance of the rail to a grind
    before it, so Flickit started it)".

The flicks go by his feet (seven builds ago)
------------------------------------------
  - As in Skate, the kickflip goes toward the skater's heels. Left foot
    forward (a regular skater in his own stance): the kickflip is down,
    flick up-left, the heelflip up-right, the pop shove-it a drag to the
    left. Right foot forward (a goofy skater, or a regular one riding
    switch): all of it mirrored, the kickflip up-right. The varials and the
    nollie flicks swap sides the same way.
  - Which foot is forward is read from the game from the moment he is on
    his board, so a level that starts with either foot forward is right
    from the start, and riding switch turns the flicks round.
  - A flick keeps the side it began on: switching stance in a crouch
    changes the next flick, not that one.
  - FlicksByFeet=0 in the [Flickit] section keeps the flicks the same
    whatever his feet (KickflipSide=0: kickflip up-right, 1: up-left).
  - With the console on, the log says which foot is forward and where the
    kickflip is ("Flickit: left foot forward (regular): the kickflip is the
    flick up-left") when he is first seen and whenever it changes.

Nollies (eight builds ago)
--------------------------
  - Push the right stick up and the skater goes into THUG's nollie stance
    and crouches, as deep as the stick is pushed (a third of the way is
    enough; further = a higher nollie).
  - Flick away from there: a nollie. The flip flicks work from up too,
    upside down, and do the nollie tricks: up, flick down-right = Nollie
    Kickflip, up, flick down-left = Nollie Heelflip, and so on. With
    Skate's skater.pat next to thugsdl.ini, Skate's own nollie flicks
    (its N_ patterns) are the ones that count.
  - Back to the centre without a flick: he stands up again, out of
    nollie. He lands out of nollie too, as in THUG.
  - The stick decides the stance: a crouch down takes him out of nollie
    if the left bumper (THUG's Nollie button) had put him there.
  - THUG has no nollie animation for the extra spin of a 360 heelflip,
    360 hardflip or 360 inward heelflip: from nollie those finish in their
    regular animation.
  - Nothing to set: it is on by default. Nollie=0 in the [Flickit] section
    turns it off (the stick up then does nothing on the ground).
  - With the console on, the log says "Flickit: the stick crouches up:
    nollie stance" and "Flickit: out of nollie stance".

The crouch you see (nine builds ago)
-------------------------------------
  - The skater crouches as deep as the stick is pulled: a little at a third
    of the way, THUG's full crouch all the way down, and anything between.
    Easing the stick back up eases him back up. CrouchPose=0 in the
    [Flickit] section gives THUG's one crouch back.

The stick (ten builds ago)
---------------------------
  - Weak flicks count, as in Skate: a crouch starts a third of the way down,
    and a flick 40 percent of the way out pops. If your thugsdl.ini already
    has a [Flickit] section, change these four lines in it (the new section
    is in flickit-ini-section.txt):
      Engage=35   Release=30   Flick=40   Snap=60
  - How far down the stick goes is how high the ollie goes (Skate's quick
    pop to its full pop).
  - The stick back to the centre without a flick: he stands up, no ollie.
  - Keep the stick where a kickflip's flick ended and it turns again:
    Double, then Triple Kickflip, if there is air to land it. The same for
    heelflips, impossibles and the 360 / 540 shove-its.

The face buttons still work, except that the Ollie button pushes while the
board rolls on the ground. The full table is in the README, section FLICKIT.

Grinds
------
Rails and ledges catch the board without a button. In the air the right stick
leans the board, and the lean at touchdown is the grind ("toward" = the side
the rail is on):

  stick at rest          50-50
  up / down              nosegrind / 5-0
  up + toward            crooked            up + away          overcrook
  down + away            salad
  to a side              boardslide or lipslide
  up, rolled toward      noseslide          up, rolled away    nosebluntslide
  down, rolled toward    tailslide          down, rolled away  bluntslide
  toward, rolled up      feeble             away, rolled up    smith

That is for a board that comes in along the rail. Coming in at an angle, the
board itself counts as the stick pushed the way its nose points (see "New in
this build" above): at rest that is a crooked when the nose points onto the
rail, a smith when the tail does.

On the rail: stick down = 5-0, up = nosegrind, let go = 50-50 (the game takes
the switch about three quarters of a second into a grind). A flick pops off;
letting go does not. Right bumper = drop off the rail. No balancing, and no
balance meter (GrindBalance=1 brings both back).

Spinning
--------
In the air the movement stick turns the skater the way Skate does.

  - How far the stick is pushed says how fast he turns. Holding it is not
    enough for much: 94 degrees in a small ollie, 127 in a full one.
  - Throw the stick over as you pop (or just before) and he turns up to two
    and a half times as fast: 220 and 301 degrees. THUG's own turning makes
    about 190 and 290 of the same two airs with left or right simply held.
  - In a long air Skate turns less than THUG: the rate falls off after the
    first second.
  - Let the stick go and the turning runs out by itself.
  - The bumpers (THUG's spin buttons) turn him the way THUG does.

  Spin=100        percent of Skate's turning. 0 = THUG's own

With the console on, every air says how hard the flick was and how far the
stick asked him to turn. Flip tricks are as they were.

Rolling
-------
The board is pushed, rolls out and steers the way Skate's does. Three parts,
three settings.

  Pushing
  - The skater no longer kicks by himself. The Flip button pushes (THUG's own
    kick button), and so does the Ollie button while the board rolls on the
    ground. In the air, on a rail and in a manual both are what they were.
    A press that pushes is not passed on to the game.
  - A tap is a small push (60 units of speed), a quarter of a second a full
    one (320). Keep the button down and he keeps pushing.
  - Pushing stops at 680 units a second, about THUG's best kick.
  - One push is one play of the game's push animation, and the speed comes
    in while its foot pushes: little as the foot starts back, most in the
    middle of its stroke, little as it arrives. The mod reads from the game
    which animation the skater is in and how far into it. No animation, no
    push: there is no speed without a foot any more.
  - Where the foot pushes, the mod finds out by watching the skater's feet
    while the animation plays: the speed comes as the foot comes down
    beside the board, slides back along the ground and goes on back as the
    leg follows through, about a quarter of a second. It knows after the
    first push of a session; that first one goes by PushFootDown and
    PushFootUp.
  - If the speed still does not sit on the foot: set Console=1 under
    [Logger] in thugsdl.ini, push a dozen times, and look for the lines
    "Flickit: watched the feet in ..." and "Flickit: push with ...". They
    say what the mod saw and what it did. With WriteFile=1 as well, what the
    console shows is also written to debug.txt in the folder the game was
    started from (WriteFile=1 does nothing without Console=1; under Program
    Files, Windows may put the file in your AppData\Local\VirtualStore
    instead). PushMeasure=0 switches the
    watching off; then PushFootDown and PushFootUp alone say where in the
    animation the foot pushes, in percent of its length.
  - After a landing, a skate-off from a rail or a bump into a wall the push
    no longer waits for that animation to end: it cuts it short, a sixth of
    a second after the landing (the game's window for a revert or a manual
    stays). The log says "Flickit: the push cut the game's ... short".
  - Crouching for an ollie comes before pushing, as in Skate: pull the stick
    back during a push and the crouch takes over as soon as the foot has
    pushed (a third of a second into the push at most, so its speed is
    kept). Down takes over at once. No push starts while you crouch; a
    button held through the crouch pushes after it. The log says
    "Flickit: the push in ... gave way to the crouch".
  - The push is shown in a turn too (THUG shows only the turn). If that looks
    wrong, PushOverTurn=0 is THUG's way: the turn is shown, and there is no
    push while the stick is held to one side.

  Rolling out
  - The board loses speed slowly, as Skate's does: from a fast roll it goes on
    for half a minute. THUG's own drag is five to seven times as strong at
    speed, which is why its skater has to kick all the time.

  Steering
  - The stick steers by how far it is pushed, a little near the centre and a
    lot at its end.
  - At a walk the board turns on the spot. The faster it is the wider it
    turns: at full speed the turn is about twice as wide as THUG's.

  Push=100        percent of Skate's push. 0 = THUG's own kick
  PushOnOllie=1   0 = only the Flip button pushes
  PushOverTurn=1  0 = in a turn the game shows the turn, and no push
  PushMeasure=1   0 = the feet are not watched, the next two say it all
  PushFootDown=8  where in the push animation the foot starts to push and
  PushFootUp=32   where it has pushed, in percent of the animation
  Coast=100       percent of Skate's rolling resistance. 0 = THUG's friction
  Steering=100    percent of Skate's grip. 200 = turns at speed about as
                  THUG does, 0 = THUG's own turning

THUG's levels expect a skater who keeps his own speed and turns sharply:
timed goals take pushing now. Each of the three can be turned back by itself.
With the console on, every push says which animation it went with, where in
it the foot pushed, how long the button was down, what it asked for and what
the speed did.

Jumps
-----
Skate's gravity in the air and Skate's pop.

  - THUG's ollie goes 45 to 75 units up (most of the skater's height) and is
    over in 0.52 to 0.67 seconds: gravity is about three times real. Skate's
    goes a fifth to two fifths of the rider's height and takes 0.56 to 0.79.
  - Now gravity in the air is Skate's (58 percent of THUG's) and every jump
    leaves the ground at 69 percent of THUG's speed. An ollie goes 37 to 61
    units up and lasts 0.61 to 0.79 seconds: four fifths as high as before,
    a fifth longer. The same goes for a boneless and a pop out of a grind.
  - Off a ramp the gravity alone counts: airs go 1.7 times as high and last
    1.7 times as long. If that is too much, turn the gravity back first.

  AirGravity=100  percent of Skate's gravity. 0 = THUG's own (it is 172)
  JumpPop=100     percent of Skate's pop. 0 = THUG's own (it is 146)
                  With AirGravity=0, JumpPop=131 keeps the jumps four fifths
                  as high as THUG's.
  CrouchPose=1    the crouch is shown as deep as the stick. 0 = THUG's one
                  crouch

How far a rail reaches
----------------------
A rail no longer pulls the board in from a metre away.

  - THUG takes any rail within 40 units of the skater's path (a metre at his
    size; 20 units when he crosses the rail), also from above and below, and
    snaps the board onto it at once. Skate only nudges a board that is about
    to pass a rail at under 24 cm.
  - Now a rail takes the board from 19 units to either side, and the board
    may be 16 units above it or 8 below. Both at once has to be nearer still.
    You have to come down on the rail.
  - A rail you have crossed or flown past does not pull you back.
  - At a ledge corner the edge under the board wins, not the edge that runs
    the way you travel.
  - Hold the Grind button for the game's own reach on that jump.

  GrindReach=100  percent of Skate's reach. 50 = as short a pull on screen as
                  in Skate (harder to hit), 200 = about THUG's own, 0 = off

With the console on, every rail says how far it reached for the board, and a
jump that lands next to a rail says by how much it missed and which
GrindReach would have caught it.

Speed on a rail
---------------
The board loses speed on a rail, as in Skate, and steps off by itself when it
has none left.

  - Metal rails slide best, ledges drag about twice as hard, rough stone and
    brick more. Least in a 50-50, 5-0 or nosegrind, most in a smith, feeble
    or crooked. From a fast roll a 50-50 lasts about eight seconds on a metal
    rail and five on a ledge; a smith on a ledge under three.
  - Out of speed, the skater steps off to the side the board came from (hold
    left or right to pick the side). On an uphill rail he steps off where
    THUG would have let him slide back down.
  - Landing on a rail no longer adds speed (THUG adds 150 every time).

  GrindDrag=100   percent of Skate's drag. 200 = Skate's distances, 0 = off
  GrindExit=1     0 = the board stays on the rail when it has stopped
  GrindBoost=0    1 = THUG's push for landing on a rail is back

With the console on ([Logger] Console=1) every grind gets a line saying what
the rail is made of, which drag that gives, and how fast the board came off.

On foot and in a car Flickit switches itself off. Both bumpers get the skater
back on the board.

A first check: coming in along a rail that is on the skater's left, hold the
stick up-left as the board touches down. That should be a crooked grind. If it comes out as an
overcrook the sides are mirrored: set GrindMirror=1 (see Settings).

If something is wrong
---------------------
- The game crashes or misbehaves in a way stock THUG-SDL did not:
  try alt-unoptimized/thugsdl.dll instead. It is the same code built with
  compiler optimization off, which is what THUG-SDL's README asks for.
  thugsdl.dll at the top of this zip is built with the compiler's default
  optimizations, which is how the DLLs shipped with THUG-SDL appear to be built.
- Grinds misbehave: put GameHooks=0 under [Flickit] in thugsdl.ini and press
  F9 in game. The mod then leaves the game's rail code alone and grinds work
  as in the build before this one (Grind held for a moment after each pop).
  GrindCatch, GrindPick, GrindSwitch and GrindBalance switch the parts one by one,
  GrindDrag=0 with GrindExit=0 gives THUG's endless grinds back,
  GrindReach=0 its own reach for rails, AirGravity=0 and JumpPop=0 its jumps,
  Push=0, Coast=0 and Steering=0 its own kick, friction and turning,
  Spin=0 its turning in the air.
- To go back to stock: delete thugsdl.dll and rename thugsdl.dll.bak back.

Skate 3 stick patterns (optional)
---------------------------------
If you own Skate 3, copy its skater.pat into the game folder, next to
thugsdl.ini. Flickit then reads the tricks from that file: each trick is a
path of stick positions, as in Skate. Without the file nothing changes.
The 360 tricks come out as the base trick tapped twice.

Settings
--------
Flickit works without touching thugsdl.ini. To change something, paste
flickit-ini-section.txt at the end of thugsdl.ini and edit the values.
F9 in game re-reads the section, no restart needed.
To see a line for every flick Flickit recognizes, set Console=1 under [Logger].
For grinds the log also says which side the rail was on, where the stick was,
the board's angle to the rail and which end pointed onto it, which grind that
made, and what the game's grind script reports.
